notes: basic_blade stays the shared swing default; these four identities play only if Codex wants a swing per weapon (P-WEAPON, M-E CP2a). No runtime key or binding is created here.

Each weapon sits in its own spectral slot (mace 450-650 Hz, dao 1050-1400 Hz, bow 1750-2400 Hz, brush 3200-4200 Hz), >=300 Hz from every sibling weapon and >=400 Hz from basic_blade (2702 Hz). Mace is told apart from metal_parry (764 Hz, prominence ~1.49M) by its low-end weight (<500 Hz band >= 0.30 vs parry 0.00) and its prominence staying below 1% of parry's (recorded, not a <200 bound: mace energy sits below 700 Hz, so the 400-2000 Hz window median is near the noise floor; same note as the grass cue in CP1).

dao_swing never plays as a fire roar and never implies gore; brush_stroke never loops bubbles and is not an impact; mace_swing is never sub-bass only (phone speakers must keep the attack); bow_string plays once per confirmed arrow release, never five sounds at once and never one big explosion for five arrows (Audio Direction v1 §1).

All loudness/true-peak/spectral numbers are measured from the real rendered bytes; no ear audition has been done. Spectral distinctness vs the ported baselines is re-measured independently by check_composed_sfx_me_cp2b_weapons_v1.py.
